children: Japan's nationwide core consumer inflation, which excludes fresh food, likely accelerated to 2.6% on year in November from 2.2% in October, mirroring the pickup in Tokyo, Barclays economists estimate. They maintain their outlook for nationwide inflation to gradually rise going forward, citing renewed increases in oil procurement costs. However, the economists note that companies are passing less of their higher labor costs on to consumers than in 2024 and 2025, meaning recent wage growth momentum is unlikely to generate meaningful second-round inflationary effects. Government data earlier Friday showed Tokyo core consumer inflation picked up to 2.9% on year in November from October's 2.6% rise. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)
